title: Interleaved attention throughput scratchpad
content:
Summary:
Quick notes from a set of exploratory runs trying to reproduce intermittent tail spikes when interleaving FlashAttention-style kernels with paged-attn fused ops. Goal: capture reproducible pattern, hypothesize root cause(s), and propose minimal microbench to isolate scheduling vs memory behavior.

Background/context:
- Symptoms observed in prod-like load: occasional 5-10x latency spikes on single-request 2k token inference with batching disabled. Mostly at p99.9 level.
- Suspected surface: interplay between fused-op kernel launches (multi-kernel opchains), GPU kernel scheduling preemption/stream syncs, and page table thrash when using pinned host staging + paged flash strategy.
- Related work: see INF-4872 and the PR above for earlier attempts that focused on kernel fusion correctness but not interleaving.

What I ran (quick reproducible harness):
- Model: distilled-22B-ish architecture clone used in serving tests (attention shapes: seq_len 2048, head=64, d_kv=64).
- HW: 1x A100-40GB, cuda 12.2 runtime, driver 535.x, nsight compute for traces.
- Builds: serving-runtime:local with DEBUG_PROF=1, fused ops enabled behind feature flag \"fuse_interleaved_attn\".
- Commands (psuedo):
  - ./bench_infer --model model.tok22b --seq 2048 --batch 1 --feature fuse_interleaved_attn --repeat 5000 --log-raw
  - ncu --target-processes all --section \"CUDA API\" --section \"LaunchStats\" -o run1.ncu ./bench_infer ...

Experiment matrix (high level):
- Varied: kernel fusion ON/OFF, pinned host staging ON/OFF, page-chunk-size (64K/256K/1M), stream concurrency (1/2/4), kernel block size heuristic (auto/manual), prefetch threads (0/2).
- Focus metric: single-request wallclock latency distribution, per-kernel launch latency, SM occupancy, GPU mem-copy bandwidth, and memcue/pagefault counters from driver.

Raw quick observations (informal):
- Baseline (no fusion, pinned staging off): stable p99 120ms, p99.9 ~140ms.
- Fusion ON + pinned off: mean slightly lower, but p99.9 jumps to 320ms intermittently (pattern: every ~300-800 requests).
- Fusion ON + pinned staging ON: average improves (fused ops amortize some overhead) but p99.9 still has spikes, sometimes worse (up to 1.2s).
- Increasing stream concurrency from 1->4 reduced frequency of spikes but individual spike magnitude unchanged.
- Page-chunk-size: small chunks (64K) increased spike frequency, large chunks reduced frequency but made spike magnitude larger when it happened.
- Nsight traces on a spike show: a burst of small memcpy operations around kernel boundary, followed by long idle on GPU prior to next kernel launch. LaunchStats show kernel queuing delay ~300-800us for some kernels.
- Driver counters show sporadic host->device page faults when pinned staging off (small blips), and higher TLB miss counters with small page-chunk sizes.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Kernel launch serialization due to implicit synchronization caused by fused-kernel interleaving with host-side prefetch completion. If we wait on a future/promise or stream synchronize implicitly, we get big tail.
2) TLB/VA pressure when using paged staging and many small page-chunks: causes device-side page faults or heavy MIGRATION -> stalls. Explains sensitivity to chunk size.
3) CUDA driver scheduling path causing round-robin stalls when many tiny memcpy + compute segments are interleaved; per-kernel enqueue cost dominates sometimes due to driver GC or context switch load.
4) Occupancy regressions due to kernel fusion variant picking lower occupancy kernels on the hot path (kernel selection bug). Less likely since occupancy plots don't show consistent drop, but still possible under certain seq lens.

Quick microbench plan to isolate (short actionable tests):
A) Pure kernel enqueue microbench: run same kernel sequence but replace memcpys with device-to-device memcopies (bypass host) and observe if spikes persist. If they go away => host staging/TLB.
B) Single stream vs multiple streams with cudaStreamAttachMemory (for pinned staging) to see if stream attachment semantics change behavior.
C) Force manual kernel fusion (merge kernels into single kernel) vs current opchain: if merged single-kernel removes spikes, then scheduling/launch overhead is culprit.
D) Kernel launch timing instrumentation: add explicit cudaEventRecord before/after every kernel + memcpy in harness and log deltas to pinpoint whether enqueue latency or kernel runtime gap occurs.

Preliminary conclusions:
- Evidence points most strongly at host staging / VA pressure and unintended synchronization points. Nsight shows memcpy + small kernel pattern that lines up with stalls. Larger page-chunk sizes reduce frequency (so fewer VA refs) but make a stall costlier when it happens.
- Multi-stream concurrency mitigates frequency but not magnitude — consistent with the idea that if one stream hits a TLB/page fault stall it blocks that work but others can proceed; magnitude still shows when the offending stream eventually resumes.

Notes / unresolved items:
- Need to correlate exact callsite that causes implicit sync (is it a cuMemcpyAsync->stream wait when memory not registered? or unpinned?) Instrument the runtime path where we stage KV cache and tag temporaries with cudaHostRegister or use cudaMallocHost.
- Need to test on different driver/cuda combos (we only tested 535/12.2). Past infra showed odd behavior on 530.x with better stability — confirm.
- Check for interactions with our custom kernel launch wrapper that may add cudaStreamSynchronize on error paths. Search for .synchronize() calls in opchain runner.

Immediate TODOs (who/when):
- Ethan: implement microbench A & D and push harness changes (INF-4872 follow-up). target: 2026-03-12.
- Priya: run test matrix on 2x A100 to check multi-GPU scatter effects (no later than 2026-03-16).
- Sofia: grep for runtime sync points and create PR to remove optimistic sync in opchain runner if found. target: 2026-03-15.

Commands / snippets for reproducing locally:
- build with small trace macro: CARGO_PROFILE=dev make bench-bin
- run: ./target/bench_infer --seq 2048 --batch 1 --repeat 10000 --feature fuse_interleaved_attn --pin-staging --page-chunk 65536 > out.log 2>&1 &
- collect events: ncu --target-processes all --trace \"kernel;memcpy;nvtx\" -o ncu-run ./target/bench_infer ...

Open questions for triage meeting:
- If this is driver/VA related, do we hard-choose larger chunk sizes in default profiles or opt for pinned staging by default? Tradeoff: memory overhead vs spike frequency.
- Is kernel fusion worth it if it increases host-side memory ops complexity? Might need a hybrid heuristic: fuse only compute kernels, keep host-copies batched.

Attachments/links (local):
- raw traces: /tmp/trace-run-2026-03-08-1/{ncu,events,logs}
- quick plot: /tmp/plots/interleaved-spike-hist.png (p99 histogram)

Last thoughts (notes to self):
- This doc is messy; keep it as a scratchpad. Aim to convert wins into a short RFC with a recommended default: either enable cudaHostRegister for staging buffers by default (if memory cost acceptable) or reduce micro-chunking and batch H2D copies per token-group.
- Logging action item: add a small telemetry counter for "enqueue_delay_ms" per request in prod debug builds so we can correlate customer-side spikes to kernel enqueue delays.
